source.title: Optimal Mini-Batch Size Selection for Fast Gradient Descent
source.authors: M. Perrone; Haidar Khan; Changhoan Kim; Anastasios Kyrillidis; Jerry Quinn; V. Salapura

record.tranche_reason: The paper studies mini-batch size and convergence time, but explicitly leaves connections to testing/generalization performance for future work. Its results do not measure the training–test gap or held-out performance as the claim versions define them.
record.gate_note: The paper reports an inverse relationship between mini-batch size and updates to reach specified training or cross-validation error thresholds. These convergence-time results do not establish held-out generalization or a training–test gap, so they are recorded under fits_no_version. Figure 1 is described as showing a trend across experiments, but only a representative subset of plots is shown.
record.test_reason: The study cites large-batch generalization research but tests convergence speed. Even where targets use cross-validation loss or test-set BLEU, it measures updates needed to reach a target, not held-out performance at a fixed epoch budget. Its results therefore test none of V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors propose an empirical inverse relationship between batch size and updates to a target, combine it with system timing to select batch sizes, and leave connections to generalization for future work.
record.recipe_differences: The paper varies mini-batch size to study convergence time and does not test the claim's held-out generalization outcomes or fixed-epoch comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported convergence relationship varies with task, model topology, learning rate, convergence threshold, and batch size; the paper notes a negative fitted N∞ for one adaptive-learning-rate experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Updates needed to reach specified loss or BLEU targets approximately follow NUpdate = N∞ + α/M across the tested tasks and conditions, with a caveat for the Adam fit.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mini-batch size predicts updates to a specified convergence target through an approximate inverse relationship in these experiments.

record.problems: The paper says Figure 1 shows only a representative subset of experiments. Most experiments were not averaged over multiple runs; MNIST experiments used ten runs, and translation combinations used five seeds. No uncertainty estimates for the reported fit are stated. The paper expressly leaves connections to generalization for future work.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for individual model and task panels were extracted: the text describes the inverse relationship as persisting across the experiments, while Figure 1 presents only a representative subset and does not provide reconstructable per-panel numeric results in the supplied text. No held-out generalization results were reported.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy under natural versus random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Held-out performance of convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD on held-out performance under specified tuning budgets.
Held-out performance across batch sizes at fixed epoch budgets, and whether recipe changes remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across training regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its association with generalization gaps.
Test accuracy after removing highly memorized versus randomly selected training examples.

record.verdict_notes: Reaching a common held-out target with different numbers of updates does not establish the held-out performance ordering at a common epoch budget. Figure 2 also omits conditions that never reached a target; these omissions do not establish a fixed-budget generalization penalty.

versions.untested_parts: Memorization of random labels and held-out performance on natural versus random labels.
Test error as network width increases beyond the interpolation threshold.
Comparative test error of convolutional and fully connected networks.
Held-out performance comparisons among adaptive optimizers and SGD.
Held-out performance at fixed epoch budgets across batch sizes, and whether recipe changes close any penalty.
The effect of dropout on held-out error.
Whether a magnitude-aware sharpness measure tracks the training–test gap.
The effect on test accuracy of removing examples the network memorizes.

rows.subject: variety of models and learning problems (representative subset of experiments shown)
rows.size_stated: varied by width and depth; see Table 1
rows.operation_detail: Varied mini-batch size and measured updates required to reach specified error thresholds.

conditions.value: MNIST, CIFAR10, CIFAR100 image recognition and Europarl machine translation
SGD; Adam used for one image-recognition model
light L2 regularization with decay constant 10−4 for image-recognition experiments
image recognition: 1–1024 for MNIST and CIFAR10; 16–1024 for CIFAR100; translation: 100, 200, 400, 800, 1600, 3200, 6400 words
varied training loss, cross-validation error, or BLEU target, depending on experiment

rows.measure: Number of updates to reach a specified training or cross-validation error threshold, or BLEU target, as a function of mini-batch size.
rows.value: The authors report that the inverse relationship NUpdate = N∞ + α/M fits the measured results across the experiments described.
rows.note: This is an aggregate finding the authors state applies across their experiments; Figure 1 shows only a representative subset. It measures convergence updates, not held-out performance or a training–test gap.
rows.check: This aggregates multiple tasks, models, learning rates and targets rather than recording individual conditions. It is valid as a summary of convergence results, but cannot establish any claim version. Cross-validation loss and test-set BLEU are held-out measures; the mismatch is the convergence-time comparison, not an absence of held-out measurements. The inverse fit also has a stated caveat: the Adam experiment yields a negative fitted N∞.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
